abstention: estimated supported dependence inside the ambiguity band returns ABSTAIN_DEPENDENCE_THRESHOLD_AMBIGUOUS and does not silently merge families
candidate_origin: R388C0017 / previously hidden parent-parent visibility surface
collapse_regions: no supported cross-family dependence edge: candidate exactly collapses to the declared CSID family partition/portfolio
supported cross-family dependence clearly below threshold: candidate collapses to declared CSID semantics
dependence already encoded by the same declared CSID evidence_family: candidate adds no new family merge and gain is zero
conservatism_boundary: connected-component family merging treats strong supported dependence as common-mode equivalence; this can be conservative for graded or antagonistic dependence and is not a copula/general dependence model
evidence_boundary: deterministic synthetic mechanism evidence only; no empirical contract-loss, reliability, market, deployment, or external scientific novelty claim
mechanism_removing_comparator: same CSID failures, safeguard costs, coverage, budget and declared evidence-family labels with covariance-based cross-family partition repair removed

nearest_existing_products.difference: EDSANP discounts correlated evidence used to justify a covariance support mask and either allows or refuses the structured-support portfolio path; it explicitly does not infer/edit the support graph. SCIG instead consumes a support-aware covariance estimate to alter CSID's downstream evidence-family equivalence partition and therefore its safeguard coverage composition/portfolio choice.
SCCATF inserts covariance cross-terms into an allocation objective. SCIG changes the independence partition that determines multiplicative safeguard coverage before portfolio evaluation.
SACAPL changes CAPL risk-objective geometry while the feasible set remains fixed. SCIG changes categorical/common-mode evidence structure used by CSID, not portfolio covariance geometry.
SCOPG uses support geometry as an identification/conditioning guard. SCIG uses support-aware covariance to merge nominally distinct evidence families inside a safeguard-dependence model.

new_failure_mode: CSID can correctly avoid double-counting safeguards that share an explicitly declared evidence_family yet still overstate independence when differently named evidence families are driven by one supported dependence channel.
non_additive_interaction: SACPS changes CSID's equivalence partition over safeguard evidence families before coverage multiplication and portfolio search. This changes the combinatorial coverage operator itself; it is not a covariance penalty appended to the same CSID objective.
support_boundary: strong raw correlation without a declared support edge is intentionally ignored; support correctness remains external and misdeclared support can still cause false merges or missed merges
working_region: nominally distinct safeguard evidence families have a supported dependence edge whose estimated absolute correlation is clearly above the declared threshold+ambiguity band; the repaired partition changes the selected CSID portfolio under the same costs, coverage and budget.
